reason: Final dependency and axiom-contract audit: For M, the O-algebra E=End_OH(M) is finite over the complete local ring O. Every element of mE is topologically nilpotent, so 1-mE consists of units by the convergent geometric series and mE lies in J(E). Successive correction and completeness lift idempotents from the finite-dimensional algebra E/mE; lifting a complete primitive orthogonal decomposition there shows that E is semiperfect. Repeatedly split nontrivial idempotents of E; positive O-rank strictly decreases, so existence terminates. If M is indecomposable, E has no nontrivial idempotent. Since idempotents lift and E/J(E) is semisimple Artinian, its decomposition has a single primitive identity, so E/J(E) is a division ring and E is local. For two finite decompositions, restrict the identity to one indecomposable summand; a finite sum equal to 1 in its local endomorphism ring has a unit term, so that summand is isomorphic to one on the other side. Split and cancel it, then induct on O-rank. This supplies the semiperfect/exchange proof directly and uses neither the published AC-stated Nakayama theorem nor the DC-stated finite-length interface. Evidence inspected: Craven, The Brauer Correspondence, Theorem 2.1 and §§2.1–2.2, pp. 18–22; Jin, Basic Modular Representation Theory, §§3–4 and Green indecomposability proof, pp. 5–7.
